9.name: appraiser inspects house thoroughly
9.description: Beverly Ostrowski moves through the house repeatedly, inspecting it room by room and taking notes with a laser.
evidence: Beverly Ostrowski moved through the house room by room, top to bottom, then bottom to top, then a second pass through the principal rooms with the laser.
She made notes.

9.name: appraiser questions household details
9.description: Beverly asks about the boiler, roof work, and rear addition while the family answers different kinds of questions.
evidence: She asked questions.
She asked about the age of the boiler, the date of the most recent roof work, the condition of the rear addition.
Rosa answered the practical questions. Daniel answered the financial questions. Lucia answered the sentimental questions

9.name: appraiser treats house as family history
9.description: Beverly's questioning reveals her understanding that the house is both a financial asset and a family fact.
evidence: Beverly was the kind of appraiser who understood that a row house in Philadelphia was both a financial asset and a fact about a family, and that the family's account of it could not change the number but could change the appraiser's confidence in the number.

9.name: appraiser gives appraisal timeline
9.description: At two o'clock, Beverly says she will provide a preliminary number by Friday and a written report the following Wednesday.
evidence: At two o'clock Beverly closed her clipboard and said she would have a preliminary number by Friday afternoon and a written report by the following Wednesday

9.name: appraiser departs after handshake
9.description: Beverly shakes hands with each family member and leaves the house.
evidence: she shook hands with each of them and let herself out

9.name: family regroups in dining room
9.description: After Beverly leaves, the four of them sit together again in the dining room.
evidence: In the dining room the four of them sat again.

9.name: Asha presents memorandum page
9.description: Asha brings only a single page listing options for the upcoming meeting and places it on the table without comment.
evidence: Asha had brought no folder this time.
She had brought only a single sheet of paper, which was the page from the memorandum that listed the options for the meeting two weeks from today, and she laid it on the table without comment.

9.name: Asha postpones discussion
9.description: Asha tells the others they do not have to discuss the issue immediately because they have until next Wednesday.
evidence: "We don't have to talk about this now," she said. "We have until next Wednesday.

9.name: Asha reframes appraisal limits
9.description: Asha explains that the report will value only the building and not speak about the family, setting up the next conversation.
evidence: But the report will not say anything about you. It will say only what the building is worth.

9.name: lawyer postpones building decision
9.description: The lawyer says the group does not need to decide what to do with the building immediately and frames the upcoming report as only about the building's value.
evidence: "We have until next Wednesday. But the report will not say anything about you. It will say only what the building is worth."
"The conversation about what to do with the building is the conversation you three are going to have, with or without me in the room, between Wednesday and the meeting the following Monday."
9.time_hint: between Wednesday and the following Monday

9.name: lawyer urges careful discussion
9.description: The lawyer suggests they begin the conversation now while she is present because people tend to speak more carefully in front of a lawyer.
evidence: "I would like to suggest that you have at least the first part of that conversation now, while I am here,"

"I have noticed in other estates that the conversations that begin in front of a lawyer tend to be slightly more careful than the conversations that begin without one, and that the careful version, once established, tends to persist."

9.name: lawyer invites Serrano to speak
9.description: The lawyer singles out Mr. Serrano and asks him to begin the discussion.
evidence: "Mr. Serrano," she said. "Would you start."

9.description: Serrano appears ready and rehearsed, but when called on he realizes his prepared response has fallen apart.
evidence: He did not look surprised to be asked.

He looked, rather, like a man who had been waiting to be asked and who had been rehearsing what he would say and who, now that the moment had come, was discovering that the rehearsal had not survived the morning.

9.name: Serrano begins reconsidering his mother's wishes
9.description: Serrano starts speaking about what he said on Monday and admits he has been rethinking his claim about what his mother would have hated.
evidence: "I have been thinking," he said.
"I have been thinking," he said, "about what I said on Monday. About my mother. About — I said she would have hated this."

9.name: Serrano admits uncertainty about mother's feelings
9.description: Serrano confesses that he no longer believes he truly knows what his mother would have hated.
evidence: "I have been thinking about that since Monday and I do not think I know what she would have hated."

9.name: Serrano distinguishes his feelings from his mother's
9.description: Serrano realizes he has been projecting his own feelings onto his mother and confusing the two for a long time.
evidence: "I think I know what I would have hated, on her behalf, and I think I have been confusing the two things for a long tim

I think I know what I would have hated, on her behalf, and I think I have been confusing the two things for a long time, and I think Lucia has known I was confusing the two things for a long time, and I think Rosa has known it longer than either of us

9.description: Daniel tells Rosa he owes her a larger apology than he can make that morning and promises to try over time.

9.description: Rosa responds that she needs the apology to be true rather than large or performative, and Daniel agrees.

"I understand."

9.name: Rosa asks to speak to the counselor
9.description: Rosa addresses Asha as counselor and asks permission to say something.
evidence: "Counselor," she said. "May I say something."
"Please."

9.description: Rosa explains that she has been thinking since Monday about what Daniel's mother wanted and separates the legal codicil from the mother's wish in the letter.

The codicil says one third, one third, one third. The letter says she wanted us to be kind. These are two different documents. They do not say the same thing. The codicil is the law. The letter is the wish."

9.name: Rosa begins to assert her long service
9.description: Rosa invokes her thirty-one years as a housekeeper to establish her authority before her thought is cut off in the excerpt.
evidence: "I have been a housekeeper for thirty-one years and I have a great deal of respect for th

9.name: distinguish codicil from letter
9.description: Rosa explains that the codicil and the letter are different documents, with the codicil carrying legal force and the letter expressing a wish.
evidence: They do not say the same thing. The codicil is the law. The letter is the wish.

I have been a housekeeper for thirty-one years and I have a great deal of respect for the difference between the law and the wish. The law is what protects you. The wish is what asks something of you. They are not enemies. But they are not the same.

9.name: Rosa rejects wanting the house
9.description: Rosa states plainly that she does not want the house, prompting Lucia and Daniel to react silently.
evidence: "I do not want the house," she said.
Lucia drew in a breath. Daniel did not move.

9.name: Rosa clarifies she cannot take the house
9.description: Rosa explains that she does not want the house in the sense of taking it from Lucia and Daniel or entering an emotionally destructive transaction.
evidence: "I want you to listen to me," Rosa said, "before you decide what I mean. I do not want the house in the sense that I cannot afford the house and I do not wish to spend my old age in a transaction with the two of you that I would not survive emotionally. I do not want the house in the sense of taking it from you. I am not capable of that and I would not become capable of it."

9.name: Rosa asks to remain in the house
9.description: Rosa says she does not want to leave and asks to keep living in her third-floor room while continuing to cook in the kitchen.
evidence: "But I do not want to leave the house either. I have lived in the third-floor room since 1996. I would like to continue to live in the third-floor room. I would like to continue to cook in this kitchen, not for wages, because I will not be a housekeeper here any longer, but because I do not know how to be in a kitchen and not cook in it."

9.name: Rosa requests a named room and key
9.description: Rosa asks that one of them keep the house and that a room be reserved for her in the legal document with her own key.
evidence: "I would like, if it is possible — and I am asking, I am not telling — I would like for one of you to keep the house. I do not care which one. I would like, in whatever arrangement you make between you, for there to be a room in it for me, named in the document, with a key that is mine and not loaned to me"

9.name: Rosa demands a room in the house
9.description: Rosa states that she wants a named room in the house, with her own key, for as long as she wants it.
evidence: I would like, in whatever arrangement you make between you, for there to be a room in it for me, named in the document, with a key that is mine and not loaned to me, for as long as I want it.

9.name: Rosa offers her share for one dollar
9.description: Rosa proposes to assign her third to whichever sibling keeps the house in exchange for one dollar.
evidence: In exchange for that, I will assign my third to whichever of you keeps the house, for one dollar.

9.name: Rosa asserts she has not consulted a lawyer
9.description: Rosa emphasizes that she has not spoken to any lawyer and is speaking on her own behalf.
evidence: I have spoken to no lawyer. I am speaking now.

9.name: Rosa insists on her right to speak
9.description: Rosa declares that she will continue speaking if anyone tells her she is wrong to do so.
evidence: I will speak again if you tell me I am wrong to speak.

9.name: Silence falls over the room
9.description: After Rosa's declaration, the room falls into an intense silence that Asha experiences as the largest she has ever heard.
evidence: There was a silence.
It was, Asha thought, the largest silence she had heard in this house, and the largest silence she had heard in any house in many years.

9.name: Lucia addresses Rosa by name
9.description: Lucia breaks the silence by speaking Rosa's name.
evidence:
Lucia spoke first.

"Rosa."

9.name: Lucia objects to Rosa's proposal
9.description: Lucia tells Rosa that she cannot make the arrangement she has proposed.
evidence: "You cannot do that."

9.name: Rosa refuses to back down
9.description: Rosa responds that she is already doing what Lucia says she cannot do.
evidence: "I am doing it."

9.name: Rosa explains her motives and family situation
9.description: Rosa explains that she is old, has family elsewhere, has enough savings, and does not want the burden of owning the building.
evidence: I am sixty-eight years old. I have a sister in Camden and three nieces and a savings account that is larger than your brother thinks it is and smaller than your sister thinks it is. I do not need a building. I need a room. The building is too much for me.

9.name: Rosa compares herself to their mother
9.description: Rosa says the house was too much for their mother as well, and that their mother never admitted it.
evidence: The building was too much for your mother and she would not say so. I am saying so.

9.name: Rosa reveals their mother asked her to prevent conflict
9.description: Rosa reveals that their mother asked her in February to keep Lucia and her sibling from destroying each other over the house.
evidence: I am saying so because she asked me, in February, to make sure the two of you did not destroy each other over this house

9.name: Rosa frames the house as belonging to one sibling
9.description: Rosa argues that the best way to avoid conflict is for the house to belong to one of the siblings rather than be split into three parts.
evidence: the way to make sure of that is for the house to belong to one of you and not to be divided into three pieces of which one piece is mine.

9.name: Rosa distinguishes legal codicil from personal wish
9.description: Rosa explains that the codicil was for legal purposes, while this conversation is about her personal wish.
evidence: The codicil was for the law. This conversation is for the wish.

9.name: Rosa explains the house should stay undivided
9.description: Rosa argues that the house should belong to one person rather than be split into three shares, framing the codicil as a legal formality and the conversation as a family wish.
evidence: sure of that is for the house to belong to one of you and not to be divided into three pieces of which one piece is mine. The codicil was for the law. This conversation is for the wish. Do you understand.

9.name: Lucia rejects Rosa's proposal
9.description: Lucia says she understands Rosa's point but refuses to accept it.
evidence: "I understand," Lucia said, "and I do not accept."

9.name: Rosa insists Lucia need not decide immediately
9.description: Rosa tells Lucia she does not have to accept the arrangement today, but Lucia repeats that she will not accept.
evidence: "You do not have to accept today."
"I will not accept."

9.name: Daniel interrupts Lucia
9.description: As Lucia begins to protest further, Daniel calls her name and interrupts the exchange.
evidence: "Lucia."
"Rosa, I will not — "
"Lucia," Daniel said.

9.name: Daniel asks Lucia to let Rosa finish
9.description: Daniel tells Lucia to let Rosa finish speaking and postpones disagreement until afterward.
evidence: "Lucia," Daniel said. He was looking at Rosa, not at his sister. "Let her finish. We can disagree with her in a minute. Let her finish what she is saying first."

9.name: Lucia falls silent
9.description: Lucia stops speaking in response to Daniel's intervention.
evidence: Lucia closed her mouth.

9.name: Rosa thanks Daniel
9.description: Rosa acknowledges Daniel's support with a brief thank-you, and he replies in kind.
evidence: "Thank you," she said.
"You're welcome."

9.name: Rosa ends her statement
9.description: Rosa declares that she is finished and invites the others to tell her she is wrong.
evidence: "I am finished," Rosa said. "That was what I had to say. Now you can tell me I am wrong."

9.name: Asha realizes she is only a witness
9.description: Asha recognizes that the discussion has shifted from legal procedure into family dynamics, leaving her outside the center of control for the first time since arriving.
evidence: She was, she realized, watching something she had not planned for and could not, in any formal sense, manage.
Rosa had taken the conversation out of the legal frame and placed it inside the family frame, and the family frame did not have rules of procedure, and Asha did not run it.
She was, for the first time since she had walked into this house on Monday morning, not the central figure in the room. She was a witness.

9.name: Asha sets down her pen and folds her hands
9.description: Asha responds by putting away her active note-taking posture and sitting back as a passive observer.
evidence: She picked up her pen, and she set it down, deliberately, on top of the single sheet of paper she had brought with her.
She folded her hands.

9.name: Lucia hesitates before responding
9.description: Lucia pauses, then speaks in a much smaller voice than before, signaling a shift from defiance to uncertainty.
evidence: Lucia spoke first, finally, in a voice that was much smaller than the voice in which she had said she would not accept.

9.name: Lucia worries about affording the house
9.description: Lucia asks Rosa what happens if she cannot afford to buy the house, revealing financial fear beneath the inheritance decision.
evidence: "Rosa," she said. "What if I cannot afford the house either."

9.name: Rosa explains the choice is not about the house
9.description: Rosa reassures Lucia that the house is secondary and explains that the codicil was meant to preserve Lucia's freedom to choose without financial pressure.
evidence: "Then your brother will keep it," Rosa said, "and you and I will visit. Or your brother will not keep it and we will all leave. The house is not the point. The room is not the point. The point is that your mother wanted you to choose. The codicil made it possible for you to choose. I am trying to make it possible for you to choose without being crushed by money. That is all I am trying to do."

9.name: Lucia asks Daniel if he wants the house
9.description: Lucia turns to Daniel and directly asks whether he wants the house, shifting the decision to him.
evidence: "Daniel," Lucia said.
"Do you want the house."

9.name: Daniel admits uncertainty about his desire
9.description: After a long silence, Daniel says he does not yet know what he wants and asks for time to figure it out before the deadline.
evidence: "I wanted to sell the house," he said finally, "and I told myself that was the same as wanting it. I think I do not know yet what I want. I think — I think I want to find out, between now and Monday week, what I want. I am asking you to let me find that out without deciding for me. I am also asking you to find out, between now and Monday week, what you want. I do not want you to tell me today. I want you to tell me when you know."

9.name: Lucia agrees to wait
9.description: Lucia accepts Daniel's request and agrees not to decide immediately.
evidence: "All right," she said.

9.name: Daniel confirms mutual agreement
9.description: Daniel echoes Lucia's acceptance, reinforcing the temporary truce between them.
evidence: "All right."

9.name: Daniel declines Rosa's offer for now

evidence: He turned to Rosa.
"Rosa," he said. "I am not accepting your offer today either. I am not refus

9.description: Lucia responds to the speaker's request by agreeing to tell him when she knows.

"All right," she said.

9.description: The speaker tells Rosa he is not accepting her offer today, but is not refusing it either.

9.name: speaker requests a week
9.description: He asks Rosa for the same week he is asking his sister for before giving an answer.
evidence: "I am asking you for the same week I am asking my sister for. Can you give it to me."

9.name: Rosa grants the request
9.description: Rosa agrees to give the speaker the week he asked for.
evidence: "I can give it to you," Rosa said.
"Thank you."

9.name: speaker asks Asha about conduct
9.description: The speaker asks Asha whether they have conducted themselves properly, using a safer question to imply concern about his own behavior.
evidence: "Counselor," he said. "Have we conducted ourselves properly."
The question was not, she understood, the question he was asking. The question he was asking was whether he had conducted himself properly.

9.name: Asha reassures the group
9.description: Asha praises their conduct, sets a Monday week follow-up, and makes herself and Marcus available by phone.
evidence: "You have conducted yourselves," she said, "better than I had any right to expect on a Thursday afternoon. We will meet again Monday week. In the meantime, I will be available by telephone at the office, and Marcus will be available by telephone at the office, and the three of you will, I hope, be available to each other."
"Yes," Daniel said.
"Yes," Lucia said.
"Yes," Rosa said.

9.name: group confirms agreement
9.description: Daniel, Lucia, and Rosa each affirm Asha's instructions and expectations.
evidence: "Yes," Daniel said.
"Yes," Lucia said.
"Yes," Rosa said.

9.name: Asha stands to end meeting
9.description: Asha rises, signaling the close of the exchange.
evidence: Asha stood.
